etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English constituten, from Latin cōnstitūtum, neuter of cōnstitūtus, past participle of Latin cōnstituō (“to put in place, set up, establish”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To set up; to establish; to enact.

quote.citation: 1651, Jer[emy] Taylor, The Rule and Exercises of Holy Living. […], 2nd edition, London:  […]  Francis Ashe […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Laws appointed and constituted by lawful authority.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To make up; to compose; to form.

quote.citation: 1779–81, Samuel Johnson, "Abraham Cowley" in Lives of the Most Eminent English Poet
quote.text: Truth and reason constitute that intellectual gold that defies destruction.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To appoint, depute, or elect to an office; to make and empower.

quote.text: Me didst Thou constitute a priest of thine.
A naughty man that will not obey the kings constitute.
